<l0/> and <l1/> accept the props of the elements they render. The other parts accept their element's attributes.

<l0/> counts against the field's `maxLength`. Only the digits that change roll. The count darkens near the limit and turns red at it, and a typed key past the limit nudges it. Screen readers hear a message when the field gets close to the limit and when it reaches it, never on every key.

<l0/> fades in once there's a value. It clears through the browser's edit history, so Cmd+Z brings the text back, and it fires your `onChange`. Escape clears too. A second Escape is left for the dialog or popover around it.

<l0/> grows with its content up to 16rem, then scrolls. The height eases between lines instead of jumping. A `block-end` addon becomes a toolbar under it, and buttons at its edges get the same inset as the corner they sit in.
<l0/> is a ghost button sized to fit inside the field. Its corners are concentric with the group's, and it gets its own focus ring.
<l0/> is skipped in the tab order because Escape does the same thing. The password toggle stays tabbable and keeps the same name, with `aria-pressed` reporting its state.

<l0/> switches a `type="password"` field to text and back. The caret and selection stay where they were, a mouse click keeps focus in the field, and the password is hidden again when the form submits. Control it with `revealed`.
A `block-start` addon sits above the field. Add `separator` to draw a hairline between them.
A disabled input dims the whole group and shows a not-allowed cursor over it. Disable addon buttons too, since they stay usable otherwise.
A plain <l0/> inside an addon is styled as a key cap. It's a visual hint only, so bind the shortcut yourself.
Addons, padding and corner radii use logical sides, so inline-start lands on the right.

The group tracks its field, so the smart parts need no wiring. <l0/>, <l1/> and <l2/> read the value, `type` and `maxLength` from the field, whether it's controlled or not.
